## Summary

This project uses machine learning to identify fraudulent credit card transactions from real-world data. The final model achieved strong performance with high business value while requiring minimal manual review.

[Download Full Report (PDF)](card_transition_report.pdf)

## Key Highlights

- **Dataset**: 98,393 transactions, 2.5% fraud  
- **Goal**: Maximize fraud detection (FDR) at top 3% risk score  
- **Model**: Tuned XGBoost  
- **Tooling**: Python, pandas, SMARTPLS, LightGBM, XGBoost


## Key Results

- **Fraud detection (FDR@3%)**:  
  `Train: 80.7%`, `Test: 76.6%`, `OOT: 57.6%`
- **Estimated savings**: $59.4 million
- **Review effort**: Only 3% of transactions flagged


## Method Summary

- Cleaned and filtered raw data (removed outliers)
- Engineered 4000+ features (velocity, ratio, digit-based, etc.)
- Selected top 20 features via forward selection (CatBoost)
- Compared 5 models → **XGBoost** outperformed others
- Identified cutoff threshold using financial value curves
